122-r1.sourceTitle: Sagitov, Weak Convergence of Probability Measures (lecture notes, Chalmers/Gothenburg)
122-r1.locator: Section 3.2 'Proof of Prokhorov's theorem' (Theorem 3.9, direct part), pp. 12-13 of the notes
122-r1.proofSketch: Given a tight family, pick compacts $K_1\subset K_2\subset\dots$ with $P_n(K_i)>1-i^{-1}$ for all $n$. The union $K_\infty$ is separable, so there is a countable class of open sets whose closures refine any open neighbourhood; form the countable class $\mathcal H$ of finite unions of $\bar A\cap K_i$. A diagonal argument gives a subsequence along which $\alpha(H)=\lim P_{n'}(H)$ exists for every $H\in\mathcal H$. Define $\beta(G)=\sup_{H\subset G}\alpha(H)$ on open sets and $\gamma(M)=\inf_{G\supset M}\beta(G)$. Seven steps show $\gamma$ is an outer measure for which closed sets are measurable and whose restriction $P$ is a probability measure (mass 1 because $K_i\in\mathcal H$), with $P(G)=\beta(G)\le\liminf P_{n'}(G)$ for open $G$, hence weak convergence.

122-r2.sourceTitle: Sagitov, Weak Convergence of Probability Measures (lecture notes, Chalmers/Gothenburg)
122-r2.locator: Section 3.1, Theorem 3.10 (Prokhorov's theorem, reverse part), p. 11 of the notes
122-r2.proofSketch: For the converse (relative compactness implies tightness on a complete separable metric space): first show that for open sets $G_n\uparrow S$ and $\epsilon>0$ some $n$ has $P(G_n)>1-\epsilon$ for all $P$ in the family, otherwise a weakly convergent subsequence $P_{n'}\Rightarrow Q$ would give $Q(G_n)\le\liminf P_{n'}(G_n)\le1-\epsilon$ for all $n$, impossible. Cover $S$ by balls of radius $1/k$, choose finitely many with mass $>1-\epsilon2^{-k}$, and take the closure of the totally bounded intersection over $k$: it is compact by completeness and has mass $>1-\epsilon$.

122-r3.sourceTitle: Hough, Math 639 Lecture 5 (slides): Characteristic functions, central limit theorems (Stony Brook, 2017)
122-r3.locator: Slides 22-25: Helly's selection theorem with proof; tight sequences definition and theorem (proof deferred to Durrett p. 104)
122-r3.proofSketch: Helly selection on the line: enumerate the rationals and by diagonalisation extract a subsequence of distribution functions converging at every rational to some $G$; set $G(x)=\inf\{G(q):q>x\}$, which is right-continuous and nondecreasing, and convergence at continuity points follows from convergence at rationals. Tightness ($\limsup_n 1-F_n(M_\epsilon)+F_n(-M_\epsilon)\le\epsilon$) is exactly the condition that every subsequential limit is a probability distribution function, ruling out escape of mass; this last equivalence is only cited, not proved, in the source.

123-r1.sourceTitle: P.J.C. Spreij, The Radon-Nikodym theorem (telegram style notes)
123-r1.locator: Section 4 Lemma 4.4 (p. 4) and Section 5 Theorem 5.1 with proof (pp. 5-6)
123-r1.proofSketch: For finite $\mu$ and finite positive $\lambda$, put $\phi=\lambda+\mu$. The functional $f\mapsto\lambda(f)$ is bounded on $L^2(\phi)$ by Cauchy-Schwarz, so Riesz-Frechet gives $g$ with $\lambda(f)=\phi(fg)$. Testing on indicators and using Lemma 4.4 (averages) gives $0\le g\le1$ a.e. The set $B=\{g=1\}$ is $\mu$-null, which splits $\lambda=\lambda_a+\lambda_s$ with $\lambda_s\perp\mu$. Rewriting as $\lambda((1-g)f)=\mu(fg)$ and testing with $f=1_{A\cap E}(1+g+\dots+g^{n-1})$, dominated and monotone convergence give $\lambda_a(E)=\mu(1_Eh)$ with $h=1_Ag/(1-g)$. The $\sigma$-finite case is by partition, then signed and complex by decomposition.
